title: OSCAR: Order-aware Scoring and Calibration for AI Rankings
abstract: arXiv:2609.24128v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Judge-specific sensitivity is useful for aggregating pairwise LLM evaluations, but its interpretation depends on which systematic presentation effects the ranking model includes. We introduce OSCAR, an order-aware framework for scoring and calibrating AI rankings, and study position as one such effect. In released judgments from 18 evaluators, the all-response A-minus-B score difference ranges from $-63.11$ to $98.31$ percentage points. Matching question text, response texts, candidate identities, and judge within the released table gives an overall difference of $24.22$ points (95% interval $[22.90,25.54]$), conditional on the released text mapping. A controlled calculation isolates the potential consequence: with true sensitivity fixed at one, omitting a position intercept of four reduces the population-optimal slope to $0.0771$. We extend sensitivity-based ranking with judge-specific position, length, and family terms, characterize

translated_title: OSCAR：面向AI排名的顺序感知评分与校准框架
translated_abstract: 评委特定的敏感性对于聚合成对的大语言模型（LLM）评估十分有用，但其解释取决于排名模型中纳入了哪些系统性呈现效应。我们提出了OSCAR，一个用于AI排名评分与校准的顺序感知框架，并将“位置效应”作为其中一种呈现效应加以研究。在来自18位评估者的已发布判定数据中，所有回答的A减B分数差异范围从-63.11到98.31个百分点。在已发布文本映射的条件下，将问题文本、回答文本、候选身份和评委进行匹配后，得到总体差异为24.22个百分点（95%置信区间[22.90, 25.54]）。一项受控计算分离了其潜在后果：当真实敏感性固定为1时，若省略大小为4的位置截距，总体最优斜率将降至0.0771。我们通过引入评委特定的位置项、长度项和家族项，对基于敏感性的排名方法进行了扩展，并对其进行了刻画……
tldr: 本文提出OSCAR框架，通过在LLM成对评估聚合中建模评委特定的位置等系统性呈现效应，实现AI排名的顺序感知评分与校准，并证明忽略位置效应会严重扭曲最优排名结果。
en_tdlr: OSCAR is an order-aware framework for scoring and calibrating AI rankings that models judge-specific presentation effects such as position, showing that omitting such effects substantially distorts the optimal aggregation of pairwise LLM evaluations.
